counting_basis: What is counted: QUESTIONS, not question-asker pairs. A question asked jointly by several members counts ONCE, not once per asker. 23,385 questions in this window were asked jointly, one of them by 47 members. The by-member files republish each joint question once per asker, so adding those files up gives a larger number than there are questions; de-duplicate on question_id before totalling anything across them. Unresolved questions: 3,472 questions in this window could not be attached to a member with confidence. They are INCLUDED in every count of questions here, because dropping them would make the totals disagree with the published record. Of those, 1,231 are PARTLY resolved: some of their askers were identified and some were not. A partly resolved question appears in the files of the askers who were identified AND is still counted as unresolved -- so a per-member total and the unresolved total deliberately overlap, and adding them is wrong. Counts of members never include a member twice.

What is counted: MEMBERS, once each. A member who served in more than one of the covered terms is counted once in each term they served, and once only within a term. A member whose party or state the source does not record is counted under an explicit 'not stated' category, never left out. So the categories always add up to the stated total membership for the term. Only party, state and number of terms served are broken down; no other personal attribute is published or counted here, and publishing one would require a recorded decision. 'Number of terms served' counts every Lok Sabha the source records for that member, including terms outside this dataset's covered window.

What is counted: QUESTIONS ATTRIBUTED TO A STATE. A question counts ONCE toward a state if at least one of its IDENTIFIED asking members holds a seat in that state -- once for the state, not once per asker, so a question asked by three members of one state is one question there. A question co-asked by members of two different states counts for BOTH, which is why adding these 36 states together gives more than the window's question total: 16,284 questions are counted for more than one state. Do not sum the states and compare the result with the published total. Questions with NO identified asking member cannot be attributed to any state and are EXCLUDED here: 2,241 questions in this window. They are still published in full in the question record and are still counted by every other aggregate; there is simply no state to attach them to, and inventing one would be worse than declaring the gap. Subjects are EXACT SUBJECT LINES as the source records them, not topics: no stemming, no case folding and no merging of near-identical lines, so two subjects differing by a word or by capitalisation are counted separately. That is what makes these counts reproducible by string equality from the published question records; grouping them into topics is a reader's judgement and would not be. Only the top 25 subject lines of each state are published; every row carries that state's whole attributable total and its distinct subject count beside it, so the figure is never read without its denominator.
